rationale: Acceptance lens (11/11 criteria, incl. AC9-11) and standards/git-workflow checks pass, but the edge-case lens's regression claim against AC5 was independently verified by reading src/utils/config.ts:209-247: resolveWorkspace() returns the global workspace wholesale as the fallback for a local profile with no local workspace object, and resolveProfileWorkspace() passes that through unmodified for local profiles. Migration 008 strips the identity trio from the global workspace entirely, so a local profile that previously inherited identity via that fallback silently loses it after this change lands — an unmitigated regression no task or test in this diff covers. Two further confirmed/plausible issues (saveProfile() full-replace risking silent identity wipe on unrelated updates; pervasive `as any` casts in the new migration violating the project's documented no-any convention) are real but independently fixable. 3 dismissed findings (statusline bypasses migrations — pre-existing, out of scope; saveMultiProviderConfig atomicity — pre-existing write pattern; splitProfileAndWorkspace default-param risk to initProjectConfig — verified unaffected, default keys unchanged) and 3 deferred (migration skip-if-any-identity-key-present is not reachable under the current pre-fix data invariant since no profile ever carried partial identity before this change; no down()/rollback for migration 008; duplicated IDENTITY_KEYS literal across config.ts and the migration file) are recorded here, not emitted as findings.

business_review.criterion: Each global profile stores and resolves its own CodeMie identity independently
Switching between global profiles applies the selected profile's own identity
Identity fields are not overwritten across unrelated global profiles
resolveProfileWorkspace() resolves identity for a global profile from profile-specific data, not shared mutable workspace state
Existing local profile behavior is not regressed
business_review.notes: CR-001: local profiles that inherit identity via the global-workspace fallback (no local workspace object defined) lose that identity once migration 008 strips it from the shared global workspace. Confirmed by reading src/utils/config.ts:209-247; not caught by any test in this diff.

business_review.criterion: Existing workspace behavior for non-identity WORKSPACE_KEYS fields remains scope-level shared
Regression coverage: two global profiles targeting different CodeMie environments resolve independently (AC7)
Regression coverage: switching back to the first global profile restores its own identity (AC8)
Migration clones shared identity onto every existing global profile, handling LegacyConfig v1 and v2 inputs
business_review.notes: v1 coverage is indirect, via loadMultiProviderConfig()'s pre-existing legacy normalization rather than an explicit v1 fixture in the new migration test.

business_review.criterion: Statusline's direct config.workspace?.codeMieUrl bypass fixed to resolve per-profile identity
Stale project-config.md contract updated to the corrected per-profile identity contract

standards_review.standard: git-workflow: commit subjects and ticket reference format
standards_review.notes: All 3 commits use Conventional Commits, reference EPMCDME-15411, end with the required attribution footer.
src/migrations/008-isolate-global-profile-identity.migration.ts casts to `as any` on every identity-key access instead of using the typed WorkspaceConfig/ProviderProfile shapes.
No secrets, raw tokens, or unsafe path handling introduced; identity fields (URL/project/integration) are not credentials.

findings.problem: Migration 008 strips codeMieUrl/codeMieProject/codeMieIntegration from the shared global workspace unconditionally, but resolveWorkspace() (src/utils/config.ts:209-221) still returns that same global workspace wholesale as the fallback for any local profile whose local config defines no `workspace` object of its own, and resolveProfileWorkspace() (lines 236-247) passes it through unmodified when isLocalProfile is true.
findings.impact: A local profile that previously inherited its CodeMie identity via the documented global-workspace fallback silently loses that identity the moment this fix's migration runs — a direct regression of AC5 ('existing local profile behavior is not regressed'). No task in plan.md and no test in this diff exercises the post-migration end state for this path; the existing test at config-project-override.test.ts:592 hand-writes identity directly into the workspace fixture rather than simulating what migration 008 leaves behind.
findings.recommendation: Needs a design decision, not a one-line patch: either (a) have local-without-own-workspace resolution also fall back to the active global profile's own identity fields (requires threading the resolved profile name into resolveWorkspace()/resolveProfileWorkspace()), or (b) explicitly scope this ticket's fix to global profiles only and document/test that a local profile must define its own workspace.codeMieUrl/codeMieProject once migration 008 has run. Add a regression test that runs migration 008 against a fixture with a local profile relying on the global-workspace fallback, then asserts the resolved identity.

findings.problem: saveProfile() replaces the whole profiles[name] object rather than merging fields into it (src/utils/config.ts, saveProfile implementation).
findings.impact: Now that codeMieUrl/codeMieProject/codeMieIntegration live directly on the profile object, any call to saveProfile() that updates an unrelated field (e.g. model or baseUrl) without re-supplying the identity trio will silently wipe that profile's previously-saved identity. This risk did not exist pre-fix, since identity lived on the shared workspace and was untouched by profile-only saves.
findings.recommendation: Merge incoming profile fields onto the existing stored profile in saveProfile() rather than replacing it outright, or explicitly carry forward existing identity fields when the caller's update omits them.

findings.problem: src/migrations/008-isolate-global-profile-identity.migration.ts uses `as any` casts on every identity-key read/write ((config.workspace as any)?.[key], (profile as any)[key], (sharedWorkspace as any)[key], (workspace as any)[key]), bypassing the WorkspaceConfig/ProviderProfile type system in a file whose entire job is correctly relocating typed fields.
findings.impact: Violates the project's documented 'no any' coding standard (AGENTS.md Coding Standards; code-quality.md). A future drift between the migration's independent IDENTITY_KEYS literal and the real WorkspaceConfig/ProviderProfile shape would not be caught by the compiler, silently miscopying a key.
findings.recommendation: Type `IDENTITY_KEYS` as `(keyof WorkspaceConfig & keyof ProviderProfile)[]` (or equivalent) and access fields through properly typed intermediate variables instead of `as any`.
